description:
## Problem

`gf2-sim` now carries three campaign execution stacks: the `executor`/`Pipeline` hybrid frame scheduler (`dvb_t2_awgn_campaign`, `ldpc_bler_sweep`), the `permanent_campaign` driver/schedule field-arm runner, and the `osd_campaign` protocol loop added by epic b7157be6. They share the data layers (canonical checkpoint writer/reader, `gf2-stats` intervals, `permanent_campaign::schema` provenance) but each owns a separate execution loop with its own parallelism and determinism mechanics. The OSD loop shipped single-threaded because nothing forced it through the existing convention (bug 258be082).

## Direction

Converge the execution layer under convention-convergence: every campaign runner drives worker parallelism and RNG determinism through the `gf2_sim::parallel` primitives (worker-offset seek, per-worker counters, ordered reduction), and the assessment names which scheduling responsibilities (work enumeration, checkpoint cadence, interruption, quarantine) can share one core across the fixed-work-item runners and the sequential-stopping OSD loop. Where semantics genuinely differ, the divergence is recorded as a named tracked exception in rustdoc, not left implicit.

## Success Criteria

- REQ-01: An assessment enumerates the three stacks' execution responsibilities and marks each as converged, convergeable (with the target primitive), or a named exception with rationale.
- REQ-02: All campaign runners obtain worker parallelism and per-worker RNG streams through `gf2_sim::parallel` or a named tracked exception cited in rustdoc.
- REQ-03: Any consolidation preserves each stack's recorded behavioral identity or re-pins fixtures explicitly in the same change.
title: Converge campaign orchestration onto shared deterministic-parallelism and scheduling primitives
